newsitem.title: USA: Portuguese wanted to keep looted gold - document.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese wanted to keep looted gold - document.

text.p: Portugal refused after World War Two to give up looted gold it received from Nazi Germany even though close to four tons of Dutch gold remained in its vaults, according to British documents released on Friday.
The 1947 documents, released by the World Jewish Congress, said Portugal refused to return the looted gold or even admit that it was looted.
In 1953, after years of pressure, Portugal gave up four tons of gold worth $5 million even though the Allies said it had received $139 million worth of gold from the Germans.

One British embassy document, dated June 2, 1947, said, "There is no possibility whatever of persuading the Portuguese to restitute the full quantity proved to have been looted as the economy of that country could not sustain such a loss. We will therefore have to be satisfied with a compromise settlement."

The document added, "Of the looted origin of the bulk of the gold in question there can be no possible doubt. The Dutch gold is, even, still in its original wrappings. Where difference of opinion has arisen is over Portugal's obligation to restore it in the same manner as other countries, e.g. Sweden and Switzerland, have undertaken to restore gold held by them in identical circumstances."
